author: Palmetto State News
title: Presbyterian men's tennis receives ITA Team Academic Award and individual honors
text:
Presbyterian men’s tennis receives ITA Team Academic Award and individual honors
The Presbyterian College Blue Hose men's tennis team was recognized on July 15 with the Intercollegiate Tennis Association (ITA) Team Academic Award for its academic performance during the 2025-26 academic year. Three student-athletes—Thomas Anderson, David Mamalat, and Dario Navarro—were also named ITA Scholar-Athletes.
To qualify for the ITA Team Academic Award, a program must achieve a team grade point average of at least 3.2 for the academic year. Presbyterian posted a team GPA of 3.38, marking its seventh consecutive season receiving this honor and the 14th time in program history.
The ITA Scholar-Athlete recognition requires individuals to have earned at least a 3.5 GPA during the current academic year. This year, 1,008 Division I men's tennis players were recognized as ITA Scholar-Athletes.
Thomas Anderson participated in 17 doubles matches this past season with various partners and recorded seven doubles wins on court three alongside Eduardo Valentin. Anderson has not declared a major and holds a cumulative GPA of 3.90.
David Mamalat was named First Team All-Big South Singles and teamed with Matija Samardzic to win the Big South Doubles title as well as earn First Team All-Big South Doubles honors. He was also selected for the Big South All-Academic team and graduated from Presbyterian College in May with a degree in Business Administration and a final GPA of 3.40.
Dario Navarro earned recognition as Big South Freshman of the Week on February 25, played in 17 singles matches—including clinching Presbyterian's win over UNC Asheville in the conference tournament quarterfinals—and competed in 21 doubles matches with several partners. Navarro has declared his major and holds a cumulative GPA of 3.67.
